s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea on exertion with prior cardiac and oncologic history
salient_findings: ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3 on ECG
Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade on echocardiogram
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Progressive dyspnea on exertion
History of multiple prior cardiac events
History of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium
Received 2 drug-eluting stents to the right coronary artery 10 months prior
Denies chest pain at presentation
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T level was 40 ng/L
ECG shows normal sinus rhythm at 90 beats per minute
ECG shows ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3
Transthoracic echocardiogram shows well-circumscribed mass in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum
Preserved left ventricular systolic function on echocardiogram
Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade on echocardiogram
Coronary angiography shows nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease

raw.rationale: The patient has a large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade on echocardiogram, which explains the progressive dyspnea on exertion and is consistent with the patient's history of metastatic disease to the myocardium.

rejected.label: myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The coronary angiography shows nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease without evidence of acute thrombotic or embolic occlusion, and the patient denies chest pain.

rejected.label: pericarditis
rejected.why: While pericarditis could explain the pericardial effusion, the presence of a well-circumscribed mass in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum suggests a more complex condition.

rejected.label: heart failure
rejected.why: The patient has preserved left ventricular systolic function on echocardiogram, which is not consistent with heart failure.

rejected.label: myocarditis
rejected.why: The patient's history and laboratory findings do not suggest an inflammatory condition such as myocarditis.
